page.layout: One printed page of running text on the right side of the scan; the left part is the binding and dark book edge. Running head at top, text in one column, no margin notes.

main_text.l: narratio dicitur, quæ rationibus est munita. Assu-
mitur aut rationes, ex rerū attributis, quas circū
stantias uocāt, ex personis, temporibus, locis, caus-
sit, factis, euentis: de quib. infrà in uerisimilib. expli-
cabit Cicero. Itē ex testimonijs, & opinione: item
ex autoritate, more, lege, religione: itē ex probata
narratis, antiquitate, memoria, fide. De testi-
monijs suo loco infrà. Opinio est, nō ex causis, &
certis principijs, sed signis collecta scientia. Autori-
tas, aut uirtute, aut fortuna parta existimatio. Lex
est, iustorū iniustorūq; distinctio, & recta ratio
in iubēdo, uetādo, et permittēdo sita. Mos, ius est,
quod aut leuiter à natura tractum, aluit, & maius
fecit usus, siue cōsuetudo. Religio est, superioris
naturæ cultus. Probitas, quæ elucet ex uitæ gene-
re integritas: ea cognoscitur ex ueritate, &
fide: confirmat etiam antiquitas, & memoria. Anti-
quitatem intelligit, antiquitatis cognitionem, &
multarum rerum usum, quæ prudētia cōtinentur:
memoriā uero eam uim, per quā animus repetit
ea quæ fuerunt. Huiusmodi enim hominibus facile
credimus, quoniā graviores putamus, quàm ut
metiri uclint, aut fallere. Sunt qui hæc duo mem-
bra coiungant: Si antiquitatis memoria, ut de O-
ratore, & in Bruto loquitur. Sed eadē propemo-
dum sententia est, ueritas autem in oratione
& conuentis cernitur: fides autem in tota uitæ con-
stantia.

page.notes: Right-hand page only; left side is binding shadow. Marginal pencil mark at lower left edge ("17.2+7") is not printed text and is omitted. Some words are doubtful in the scan due to the curved gutter, notably "stantia" in the catchword position, which is printed as the last line and therefore not a catchword; the catchword element is a duplicate and may be removed.
